definition: Eating the right variety and amount of different foods.
business_context_example: A balanced diet beats any supplement you can buy in a shop.

definition: How much food you put on the plate at one time.
business_context_example: She changed nothing except portion size and lost 6 kilos.

definition: A unit measuring the energy in food.
business_context_example: A large latte has more calories than a slice of bread.

definition: A substance in food that the body needs to work well.
business_context_example: Frozen vegetables keep most of their nutrients.

definition: A nutrient that builds and repairs the body.
business_context_example: Most people eat enough protein and worry about it anyway.

definition: A nutrient that gives the body energy, found in bread, rice and pasta.
business_context_example: Cutting every carbohydrate is why most diets last eleven days.

definition: The part of plant food that helps digestion.
business_context_example: Beans, oats and apples are cheap sources of fibre.

definition: A type of fat that should be limited for heart health.
business_context_example: Butter and cream are high in saturated fat.

definition: Made using the whole grain, keeping more nutrients.
business_context_example: Swap white bread for wholegrain and you've done something real.

definition: Food changed from its natural state, often with added salt or sugar.
business_context_example: Not all processed food is bad, but the ready meals usually are.

definition: A pre-cooked meal you only need to heat.
business_context_example: Two ready meals a week is fine; two a day is a different story.

definition: Made at home rather than bought ready to eat.
business_context_example: A home-cooked meal takes 20 minutes if you plan it on Sunday.

definition: A meal bought from a restaurant to eat elsewhere.
business_context_example: Friday takeaway is a habit, not a decision, and that's the problem.

definition: Made mainly or completely from plants.
business_context_example: He eats plant-based four days a week and doesn't call it anything.

definition: Containing no milk products.
business_context_example: The café has three dairy-free options now.

definition: Containing no gluten, the protein found in wheat.
business_context_example: Gluten-free matters medically for about 1% of people.

definition: Unable to digest the sugar in milk properly.
business_context_example: She's lactose intolerant, so oat milk for her coffee.

definition: The information printed on packaging about what is inside.
business_context_example: Read the food label from the bottom: the sugar is hiding there.

definition: How much sugar a food contains.
business_context_example: The sugar content of that yoghurt is higher than a chocolate bar.

definition: Sugar put into food during production, not naturally present.
business_context_example: Added sugar appears under six different names on labels.

definition: Containing less fat than the standard version.
business_context_example: Low-fat often means more sugar, so check both numbers.

definition: How much of a nutrient you should have in a day.
business_context_example: One glass covers half the recommended daily amount of vitamin C.

definition: To eat or use less of something.
business_context_example: I've cut down on coffee, not cut it out. There's a difference.

definition: To stop eating something completely.
business_context_example: He cut out fizzy drinks in January and hasn't gone back.

definition: In sensible, limited amounts.
business_context_example: Cake in moderation is a plan. Cake never is a fantasy.

definition: Preparing several meals in advance.
business_context_example: Two hours of meal prep on Sunday saves five bad lunches.

definition: To not eat when you normally would.
business_context_example: Skipping lunch usually means eating twice as much at seven.

definition: A small amount of food eaten between meals.
business_context_example: Keep a decent snack in the drawer or the vending machine wins.

definition: To eat more than the body needs.
business_context_example: It's easy to overeat when you're watching something.

definition: Eating because of emotions rather than hunger.
business_context_example: Comfort eating isn't a discipline problem, it's a stress problem.

definition: Paying attention to your food while you eat it.
business_context_example: Mindful eating mostly means putting the phone down.

definition: To want a particular food very strongly.
business_context_example: I crave salty food when I haven't slept.
translation_bg: да ми се яде силно нещо

definition: The desire to eat.
business_context_example: Stress kills my appetite, then it comes back at midnight.

definition: Managing how much you eat at each meal.
business_context_example: A smaller plate does more for portion control than willpower.

definition: To drink enough water through the day.
business_context_example: Stay hydrated: half of what feels like hunger at four o'clock isn't.

definition: To become heavier.
business_context_example: I put on four kilos during the winter and it wasn't a mystery.

definition: To become lighter.
business_context_example: She lost weight slowly, which is the only way it stays off.

definition: To pay attention to your food choices.
business_context_example: I watch what I eat on weekdays and relax at the weekend.

definition: A popular diet that promises fast results and rarely lasts.
business_context_example: Every January brings a new fad diet and the same outcome.

definition: Repeatedly losing and regaining weight.
business_context_example: Yo-yo dieting is harder on the body than staying steady.
translation_bg: постоянно сваляне и качване на килограми

definition: A change you can keep doing for years.
business_context_example: A sustainable habit is boring, and that's exactly why it works.

definition: How quickly the body turns food into energy.
business_context_example: Metabolism slows with age, but far less than people claim.

definition: To break down food in the body.
business_context_example: Some people digest dairy fine, others really don't.

definition: The condition of the bacteria and system that digest food.
business_context_example: Gut health improves with fibre long before any supplement.

definition: The level of sugar in the blood.
business_context_example: A big lunch spikes your blood sugar and then the afternoon is gone.

definition: A vitamin or mineral taken in addition to food.
business_context_example: A supplement fills a gap, it doesn't replace a meal.

definition: A substance the body needs in small amounts to stay healthy.
business_context_example: Most people here are short of vitamin D in February.

definition: A written list of what to buy.
business_context_example: A shopping list is the cheapest diet tool that exists.

definition: To have a meal at a restaurant instead of at home.
business_context_example: We eat out twice a month now instead of twice a week.

definition: Something enjoyable eaten occasionally, not daily.
business_context_example: If it's a treat every day, it stopped being a treat.
